1. # **Introduction**

   1. ## **Purpose** 

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document defines the complete functional and non-functional requirements for the Hotel Reservation and Guest Services Management System (HRGSMS) to be developed for SkyNest Hotels (Pvt) Ltd. The HRGSMS will replace the existing outdated desktop-based reservation system with a unified, web-based platform that supports room bookings, guest check-in/check-out processing, chargeable service tracking, automated billing, and management reporting across all three hotel branches located in Colombo, Kandy, and Galle, Sri Lanka.

This document serves as the authoritative reference for all stakeholders involved in the design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance of the HRGSMS. It establishes clear, testable, and unambiguous requirements that guide the engineering team and form the basis for system acceptance. The document contains added functionality such as guest being registered as members and put into specific tiers to ensure to improve hospitality and operational profitability of sky nest hotels.

4. ## **Product Scope**

The HRGSMS is a unified hotel management platform designed for SkyNest Hotels, a regional hotel chain operating in Sri Lanka. The system addresses critical operational failures in the existing desktop-based system, including overbooking, billing delays, and manual data-entry errors.

Business Objectives:

●       Eliminate double-booking through real-time room availability enforcement

●       Automate billing calculations including room charges, service charges, and applicable taxes

●       Provide centralized management of guest records, bookings, and services across all three branches

●       Generate accurate management reports for occupancy, revenue, and service analytics

●       Ensure ACID-compliant database transactions for financial integrity

 

System Boundaries \- In Scope:

●       Room inventory management (branches, room types, availability)

●       Guest registration and booking lifecycle management

●       Check-in and check-out processing

●       Chargeable guest service tracking

●       Billing, payment processing, and outstanding balance management

●       Five management report types

System Boundaries \- Out of Scope:

●       Online customer-facing booking portal (external website)

●       Integration with third-party OTA platforms (Booking.com, Expedia)

●       Payroll and HR management

●       Inventory/purchasing management for hotel supplies

2. # **Overall Description**

   1. ## **Product Perspective**

The HRGSMS is a new, standalone hotel management system replacing the existing manual desktop-based application currently used by SkyNest Hotels. It is not a component of a larger existing system. The system will operate as a centralized web application accessible from workstations at all three hotel branches via a local area network (LAN) or secure VPN connection.

The high level architecture comprises the following layers:

●       Presentation Layer \- Web-based UI accessible through modern browsers

●       Application Layer \- Business logic, validation, booking rules, billing engine

●       Database Layer \- Relational database (MySQL 8.0) with stored procedures, functions,      and triggers

●       Reporting Layer \- Pre-built parameterised reports accessible to management users

2. ## **Product Functions**

*The following summarises the major functional capabilities of HRGSMS:*

●       Hotel Branch and Room Management \- Manage three branches, room categories,    types, rates, and amenities

●       Guest Management \- Register, search, and maintain guest profiles

●       Reservation Management \- Create, modify, and cancel room bookings with conflict detection

●       Check In Processing \- Validate booking, update room status to Occupied, record check-in timestamp

●       Check Out Processing \- Calculate final bill, validate payment, update room status to Available

●       Guest Service Management \- Log and price chargeable services during guest stay

●       Billing and Payment \-Generate itemised invoices, record payments, track outstanding balances

●       Partial Payment Support \- Allow multiple payments against a booking; flag unpaid dues

●       Double-Booking Prevention \- Enforce room availability via constraint checks and triggers

●       Management Reporting \- Generate five report types on demand

●       Audit Trail \- Log all system events for compliance and accountability

   5. ## **Design and Implementation Constraints**

The design and implementation of the HRGSMS are governed by the following constraints:

* **Database-First Architecture & ACID Compliance:** MySQL 8.0 is the backbone of the database centric design . All critical business logic—specifically check-ins, billing calculations, and double-booking checks—must be executed within MySQL using stored procedures, functions, and triggers. Application-layer code must not be the sole arbiter of system state.  
* **Data Integrity & Normalization:** All database relations must be normalized to **Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)** to eliminate redundancy and prevent anomalies. Referential integrity must be strictly enforced at the schema level using Foreign Keys with explicit ON DELETE RESTRICT or ON DELETE CASCADE rules. Primary keys, unique constraints, and check constraints are mandatory throughout the schema.  
* **Technical Stack:** Core database operations and critical business logic must be executed using SQL via MySQL 8.0 stored procedures and triggers to guarantee ACID compliance. The application-layer framework is fully centralized on a JavaScript/Node.js stack, specifically utilizing Node.js v20.x alongside Express.js and Next.js. This open-source architecture, paired with deployment on Cloudflare's serverless edge platform (Cloudflare Pages/Workers), is strictly utilized to minimize licensing costs while maximizing global scalability and eliminating cold start delays   
* **Performance:**  
  * **Reporting:** Reports must complete within 10 seconds for data spanning up to 1 year.  
  * **Transactions:** Booking creation response times must be within 2 seconds.  
  * **Indexing:** Appropriate indexes (e.g., B-Tree) must be implemented on frequently queried columns, including booking dates, room status, and guest IDs.  
* **Security & Regulatory Compliance:**  
  * **Authentication:** Passwords must be hashed using bcrypt.  
  * **Encryption:** All communications must be encrypted over HTTPS/TLS 1.2+.  
  * **Data Protection:** Parameterized queries are mandatory to prevent SQL injection. The system must comply with the *Sri Lanka Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022* and *PCI DSS* standards for payment data.  
* **Audit & Logging:** All financial transactions and booking status changes must be logged with timestamps and user IDs.  
* **User Interface:** A functional UI is required; however, database design quality, data consistency, and referential integrity remain the primary deliverables of the project.

  7. ## **Assumptions and Dependencies**

**Assumptions**

* **Business and Operational Rules:**  
  * SkyNest Hotels will maintain consistent operational procedures across all three branches (Colombo, Kandy, Galle).  
  * Staff roles and responsibilities are clearly defined and consistent with the system's Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) structure.  
  * All financial transactions and payments are strictly processed and recorded in Sri Lankan Rupees (LKR).  
  * Standard check-in time is assumed to be 2:00 PM, and standard check-out time is 12:00 PM.  
  * A room can only have one active booking for overlapping dates; database constraints will forcefully prevent double-booking.  
  * Service prices are fixed at the exact time of usage to prevent historical billing discrepancies if the catalogue is updated later.  
  * The final billing formula assumes a fixed sequential statutory tax structure: 10% Service Charge (SC), 1% Tourism Development Levy (TDL), 2.5% Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL), and 18% Value Added Tax (VAT).  
* **Data Population and Migration:**  
  * The database will initially be populated with sample data representing the three hotel branches, room inventory, service catalogue, and sample guest bookings to rigorously test ACID compliance before deployment.  
  * Manual data entry will be performed to set up initial hotel configurations, including room types, pricing structures, service offerings, and staff user accounts.  
  * Historical booking data from the legacy desktop-based system will be migrated to the new centralized database where feasible to maintain guest loyalty ledgers and preferences.  
* **User Authentication and Security:**  
  * Implementation of robust user authentication mechanisms with role-based access control isolating branch-specific data.  
  * Newly registered internal employee accounts will undergo manual verification and approval by an IT Administrator before system access is granted.  
  * Multi-factor authentication may be required for administrative users and financial transaction processing.  
* **Regulatory Compliance:**  
  * Adherence to the Sri Lanka Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022, as well as international standards for handling guest information.  
  * Compliance with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS v3.2.1) for processing credit card payments.  
  * Guest data retention and privacy policies align with local hospitality industry standards.  
* **User Training and Adoption:**  
  * Hotel staff will receive comprehensive training on the new system, including reservation management, check-in/check-out processes, service request handling, payment processing, and report generation.  
  * New reception staff will be able to perform standard hotel operations after one working day of training.  
  * Ongoing support and refresher training programs will be available to ensure high system adoption.

**Dependencies**

* **Integration with Existing Systems & External APIs:**  
  * Integration with the current desktop-based booking system for data migration.  
  * Integration with point-of-sale (POS) systems at hotel restaurants and bars.  
  * Integration with accounting software for financial reporting and reconciliation.  
  * **OTA Integration Status:** While the system architecture includes channel manager API hooks (SI-08), **direct integration with third-party platforms like Booking.com or Expedia is excluded from the current v1.0 release scope** unless explicitly specified by SkyNest management. The current version will rely on modular webhooks to facilitate these integrations in future phases .  
  * The system depends on the PayHere Checkout API (and its webhook callbacks) to securely process credit/debit card transactions and validate final bills .  
  * Automated email dispatch depends on third-party SMTP gateways (e.g., Nodemailer, SendGrid, Resend) .  
* **Technology Stack and Infrastructure:**  
  * The system's core reliability is heavily dependent on MySQL 8.0; all critical business logic (billing calculations, overlap prevention) depends on database-level stored procedures, functions, and triggers executing correctly.  
  * Application hosting and performance depend on Cloudflare Pages/Workers (V8 Edge Runtime) to handle global serverless computing, routing, and zero cold-start API executions.  
  * Changes to these chosen open-source technologies could impact system development timelines and performance.  
* **Network and Infrastructure:**  
  * Continuous operation depends on reliable internet connectivity at the Colombo, Kandy, and Galle branches, maintaining a minimum 10 Mbps LAN connection to interface with the cloud backend.  
  * Backup internet connections at the branches are required to prevent booking disruptions during network outages.  
  * Mobile device compatibility is strictly required for staff using tablets or smartphones for agile guest services.  
* **External Dependencies:**  
  * Third-party service availability (payment gateways, edge deployment platforms) maintaining high uptime and reliability.  
  * Internet banking and payment processing services compatible with the Sri Lankan financial system.

3. # **External Interface Requirements**

   1. ## **User Interfaces** {#user-interfaces}

### 

The user interface of the Hotel Reservation and Guest Services Management System (HRGSMS) is built using React v18.x (Next.js v14.x Client Components) to deliver a dynamic, cross-platform experience. The interface includes the following core modules and features:

**1\. Authentication & Registration Screens**

* **Unified Access:** All users (guests and staff) access the system via unified, secure authentication pages.  
* **Guest Onboarding:** Unregistered users are presented with a streamlined registration form to join the "SkyNest Luxury Reserve" loyalty program, capturing essential profile data .  
* **Role-Based Routing:** Upon successful login, the system automatically redirects users to role-specific dashboards based on their credentials and assigned hotel branch (e.g., Colombo, Kandy, or Galle). 

The following dummy image reflects the expected login page functionality planned to be implemented

![][image3]

**2\. Role-Specific Dashboards**

* **Guest Portal:** Registered members can manage their personal profiles, book rooms, track their loyalty points (Silver/Gold/Platinum), and access seasonal discounts .  
* **Front Desk Dashboard:** Receptionists can manage localized branch reservations, execute check-ins/check-outs, log chargeable services, and process payments.  
* **System Administrator & Manager Dashboard:** IT Admins and General Managers have access to global configurations. This interface provides real-time system uptime metrics, API interface health (e.g., OTA synchronizations), staff role management, and centralized property configurations across all three branches.

**3\. Reservation Management**

* **Accessibility:** Available to Front Desk staff, Hotel Managers, and System Administrators .  
* **Functionality:** Users can add new reservations, view existing bookings, modify guest details, and handle cancellations .  
* **Conflict Prevention:** The interface actively queries the database to display real-time room availability, visibly restricting overlapping dates to prevent double-booking.

**4\. Guest Services Management**

* **Usage Tracking:** Front desk staff and service personnel can log chargeable amenities to a specific active booking .  
* **Dynamic Pricing:** The interface locks in the current price of a service from the catalogue at the exact time of usage to ensure accurate progressive billing.

**5\. GUI Standards & Accessibility**

* **Tailwind CSS:** The application interface relies on the Tailwind CSS v3.4.0 framework for responsive layout rendering . This ensures seamless viewing adaptability across mobile devices (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) and desktop workstations (Windows, macOS) .  
* **Accessibility Compliance:** The UI uses clear fonts, appropriate color contrast, and keyboard navigation support to ensure usability for front-desk staff in fast-paced environments.

**6\. Standard Interactive Elements**

4. **Primary Actions:** Standard buttons include "Book Room", "Cancel Booking", "Check In", "Check Out", "Submit Payment", and "Log Service".  
5. **Administrative Actions:** Privileged users have access to advanced controls such as "Sync OTA", "Configure Gateway", "Add Property", and "Generate Revenue Report".

## **3.1 Hardware Interfaces**

Since the Sky Nest Hotel Reservation and Guest Services Management System (HRGSMS) is developed as a modern, web-based application utilizing a serverless edge architecture, it does not require direct low-level interaction with custom or proprietary hardware components. All hardware interactions are mediated by the host operating systems and standard web browsers.

The system shall interface with the following physical hardware components:

6. **Client Workstations (Front Desk & Back Office):**  
   1. The software interfaces with standard computer peripherals (keyboards, mice, and displays) through web browsers.  
   2. Client workstations must meet the minimum hardware specifications of a dual-core CPU and 4 GB RAM .  
   3. The display hardware must support a minimum screen resolution of 1366x768 for optimal rendering of the application's user interface .  
7. **Mobile Devices (Guests & Management):**  
   1. The responsive web interface accommodates standard mobile hardware (touchscreens) on iOS and Android devices, dynamically scaling to fit various viewport dimensions.  
8. **Networking Hardware:**  
   1. The application relies on standard local area network (LAN) hardware (routers, switches, firewalls) at the Colombo, Kandy, and Galle branches to maintain an active internet connection.  
   2. The network hardware must sustain a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps LAN to guarantee uninterrupted transmission of HTTPS requests to the Cloudflare edge network.  
9. **Server Infrastructure:**  
   1. Physical application server hardware is entirely abstracted by Cloudflare’s global edge network infrastructure.  
   2. The underlying host hardware for the MySQL database must meet the minimum physical server requirements of a 4-core CPU and 16 GB RAM to process concurrent transactions and analytical reporting queries

### The following software interfaces were chosen to keep in compliance with the place of deployment of the product.

### **Architectural Justification: Why Cloudflare was Chosen for Deployment**

Deploying the SkyNest Hotel Reservation and Guest Services Management System (HRGSMS) on **Cloudflare (Cloudflare Pages / Workers)** provides significant technical and operational advantages over traditional monolithic cloud hosting:

1. **Ultra-Low Latency via Edge Proximity (Sri Lanka & Global Reach):**  
   * Traditional cloud servers are anchored to specific physical data centers (e.g., AWS Singapore or India). Cloudflare runs code on an extensive global edge network spanning over 300 cities worldwide (including local edge infrastructure in Colombo, Sri Lanka).  
   * This ensures that both local hotel staff in Colombo, Kandy, and Galle, as well as international guests accessing the system via Agoda or Booking.com, experience near-instantaneous page load speeds (FCP $\< 0.5\\text{ seconds}$).  
2. **Serverless Node.js Compatibility & Zero Cold Starts:**  
   * Cloudflare Workers utilize lightweight V8 isolate engines rather than heavy container virtualizations. This eliminates "cold start" delays, ensuring that JavaScript/Node.js API routes (such as immediate room availability checks or billing calculations) execute in milliseconds under high concurrent traffic.  
3. **Enterprise Security & DDoS Protection at No Extra Cost:**  
   * Hotel booking platforms are high-value targets for automated scraping, credential stuffing, and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Cloudflare provides built-in Layer 3/4/7 DDoS mitigation, Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules, and automated SSL/TLS termination, shielding the underlying backend database from direct public exposure.  
4. **High Availability and Infinite Scalability for Seasonal Peaks:**  
   * During peak tourist seasons or promotional campaigns, booking traffic can spike unexpectedly. Cloudflare's serverless infrastructure scales compute resources dynamically across its global network without requiring manual server provisioning, infrastructure management, or downtime.

Out: Real-time room availability counts, daily rate updates, restriction rules. | Automated webhook parsing, property ID mapping, inventory conflict checks to prevent double-bookings. | Bi-directional HTTPS REST/XML Webhooks with HMAC signature verification for API security. |

## 

### **3.4 Communications Interfaces**

* ***N*****etwork Protocols:**  
  * **HTTP/HTTPS & HTTP/3:** Asynchronous HTTP/HTTPS is the primary protocol for REST API communication between the React/Next.js frontend interfaces and the Node.js backend services.  
  * **Edge Routing:** HTTPS is mandatory for all connections to ensure guest data privacy, leveraging Cloudflare's automated HTTP/3 protocol negotiation.  
* **Security Protocols & Compliance:**  
  * **TLS/SSL:** All data in transit must be encrypted utilizing Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or higher. This is actively managed via Cloudflare’s edge-level SSL/TLS termination.  
  * **Regulatory Compliance:** Payment processing and data handling must strictly comply with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS v3.2.1) .  
  * **Local Privacy Laws:** All guest personal information communication must comply with the Sri Lanka Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022\.  
* **Web Services & External APIs:**  
  * **API Security:** These channel manager integrations require HMAC signature verification for API security.  
  * **Email Gateway API:** Outbound SMTP and HTTPS API communications using OAuth2/API Key authentication are required for sending transactional emails (e.g., tier-change notifications, invoices) via Nodemailer, SendGrid, Resend, or breVO.  
* **Synchronization & Real-Time Communication:**  
  * **Database Synchronization:** Database communication operates via an encrypted TCP/IP socket connection using the standard MySQL wire protocol. This is facilitated via Prisma ORM or the mysql2 driver to maintain consistent room availability across the Colombo, Kandy, and Galle branches.  
  * **Payment Synchronization:** Server-to-server POST requests and webhook callbacks (notify\_url) via the PayHere Checkout API ensure immediate payment status verification, simulated partial payment processing, and final check-out bill validation.  
  * ***Inventory Synchronization:*** Automated webhook parsing and property ID mapping immediately synchronize room status updates and restriction rules across all systems to strictly enforce the prevention of double-booking

Optionally **OTA Integration (Webhooks)** Bi-directional HTTPS REST/XML Webhooks can be utilized for automated two-way inventory and reservation synchronization with external Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) if Agoda and [Booking.com](http://Booking.com) are planned to be connected, using their Open APIs. Functionality for External bookings will not be implemented unless requested to.

## **4\. System Features**

This section defines the functional requirements of the system using a combined organizational approach, first defining the primary System Actors (User Classes) and Entities (Object Classes), followed by the specific functional modules and their stimulus/response behaviors.

### **4.1 System User Classes (Actors)**

The system distinguishes between several user classes, each with specific access privileges. The functional features detailed in sections 4.3 through 4.8 dictate how these specific users interact with the system.

 As the System User classes were defined under section 2.3 under user characteristics the necessary tables were not included under here. Please refer to section 2.3 as necessary. However it is important to deem the functional requirements of the actors in the system.

#### **4.1.1 User Role Functional Requirements**

To enforce the permissions outlined in the actor definitions, the system shall implement the following baseline role capabilities:

* **REQ-ACT-01 (Unregistered Scope):** The system shall permit unauthenticated users to view global room availability, view baseline daily rates, and execute standard guest checkout transactions.  
* **REQ-ACT-02 (Member Scope):** The system shall permit authenticated Members to view their historical and upcoming bookings, cancel eligible active bookings, and view their current loyalty tier and point expiry ledger.  
* **REQ-ACT-03 (Front Desk Scope):** The system shall restrict Front Desk Staff to executing CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations *only* on bookings, room statuses, and billing ledgers associated with their explicitly assigned hotel branch.  
* **REQ-ACT-04 (Manager Scope):** The system shall permit Hotel Managers to modify the local branch service catalogue pricing and generate localized branch revenue reports, but shall deny them access to global system configurations.  
* **REQ-ACT-05 (Admin Scope):** The system shall permit System Administrators to view multi-branch aggregated reports and manage all employee accounts, but shall log all Admin-level data mutations for security auditing.

**4.2 System Object Classes (Entity Mapping)**

To ensure the functional requirements align directly with the database-centric design, system operations manipulate the following core Object Classes, which enforce specific business logic and regulatory compliance:

* **The Room Object:**  
  * **Role:** Represents physical inventory.  
  * **Constraints:** Maintains its state (`Available`, `Occupied`, `Cleaning`, `Temporarily Closed`). It is heavily read during availability checks but relies on the `Booking` object's ACID transaction locks to prevent concurrent modification errors.  
* **The Booking Object:**  
  * **Role:** The central transactional hub linking a Guest, a Room, and a time period.  
  * **Constraints:** Creation is strictly guarded by the `sp_CreateBooking` stored procedure to enforce zero double-bookings. It cannot transition to a `Checked-Out` state until the linked `Bill` object reflects a 0.00 outstanding balance.  
* **The Service Object:**  
  * **Role:** Represents chargeable amenities (e.g., Laundry, Minibar).  
  * **Constraints:** When instantiated as a "Service Usage" log on a booking, it dynamically locks in the *current* catalogue price, immunizing historical guest bills from future catalogue price updates.  
* **The Bill Object (Financial & Tax Ledger):**  
  * **Role:** Aggregates all financial data for a stay and acts as the strict enforcer of Sri Lankan statutory tax compliance.  
  * **Constraints:** The object strictly relies on the database stored procedure (`sp_Generate_Final_Bill`) to calculate the progressive total. It guarantees the sequential application of mandatory levies on the base charge (Room \+ Services): **10% Service Charge (SC)**, **1% Tourism Development Levy (TDL)**, **2.5% Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL)**, and **18% Value Added Tax (VAT)**. It also manages the subtraction of partial payments.  
* **The Guest Profile Object (Loyalty Ledger):**  
  * **Role:** Maintains the identity, contact preferences, and loyalty status of registered users.  
  * **Constraints:** Listens for completed payment events to dynamically increment points. It enforces the strict 1-year point expiration rule via a background CRON job, automatically downgrading tier statuses if points expire without recent stays.

### 

### **4.3 User Authentication and Access Control**

**4.3.1 Description and Priority** High Priority. This module handles secure registration, credential-based login, and strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). It ensures external guests can easily onboard while enforcing rigid IT oversight over internal employee accounts.

**4.3.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* **Guest Registration:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A guest registers via the website, providing an email and password.  
  * **Response:** The system immediately creates an active Guest Profile Object.  
* **New Employee Registration & IT Approval:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A newly hired receptionist registers for a staff account.  
  * **Response:** The system creates the account but flags it as "Pending Approval," actively denying system login.  
  * **Stimulus:** The IT Admin logs in, verifies the employee, assigns the "Front Desk" role for a specific branch, and approves the account.  
  * **Response:** The system activates the account, granting localized branch access.  
* **Past or resigned employee login**  
      **\-   Stimulus**: An employee who has resigned, or who is inactive for a given certain period of time  tries to login to the system, the System   
      \-    **Response**: the IT admin is notified and denies the request to login, if the employee has resigned or if the employee has not marked as present in the work register to the workplace recently or on present day is denied entry. The resigned employee’s account would be deleted afterwards**.**  
*  **Forgot Password**  
  *   Stimulus: A user must be able to user select the "Forgot Password" option and enter their registered email address.  
  *  Response: The system sends a secure password reset link to the user’s email.

**4.3.3 Functional Requirements**

* **REQ-AUTH-01:** The system shall allow guests to independently register for member accounts.  
* **REQ-AUTH-02:** The system shall require all newly registered internal employee accounts to be manually verified and approved by a designated IT Administrator before login access is granted.  
* **REQ-AUTH-03:** The system shall require registered internal employee accounts that have been inactive or appear to be not employed any longer has to be manually verified i(if return back to work; example : after leave) or be denied and deleted  
* **c** The system shall enforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), isolating branch-specific data (e.g., room availability, local check-ins) for Front Desk Staff, while providing Upper Management and IT Admins a global, cross-branch view.  
* **REQ-AUTH-05:** allow users to change password and make sure necessary verification is done.

### **4.4 Reservation Management**

**4.4.1 Description and Priority** High Priority. This core module handles the creation, modification, and tracking of room reservations. It supports direct bookings and integrates with Online Travel Agencies (OTAs). It relies on database-level ACID transactions to ensure zero double-bookings.

**4.4.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* **Direct Booking Search:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A user selects dates and a preferred branch on the web interface.  
  * **Response:** The system queries the database and displays available rooms.  
* **Guest Checkout vs. Member Registration:**  
  * **Stimulus:** An unregistered user proceeds to finalize a booking.  
  * **Response:** The system prompts the user with an explicit option to register as a member to earn points for this stay, or allows them to proceed with a one-time "Guest Checkout."  
* **Member booking:**  
  * **Stimulus:** An registered user proceeds to do a booking.  
  * **Response:** The system queries the database and displays available rooms, allows user to use reward points and apply available offers according to the member’s tier and availability.  
* **Overlapping Booking Attempt:**  
  * **Stimulus:** Two users attempt to book the exact same room for overlapping dates simultaneously.  
  * **Response:** The database trigger (`trg_Prevent_Double_Booking`) fires, committing the first transaction and prompting an "Unavailable" error to the second user.

**4.4.3 Functional Requirements**

* **REQ-RES-01:** The system shall allow direct room bookings without an account (Guest Checkout), while explicitly prompting users with an option to register as a member during the checkout flow.  
* **REQ-RES-02:** The system shall execute booking creation via an isolated database transaction to guarantee ACID compliance.  
* **REQ-RES-03:** The system shall automatically reject any booking attempt that overlaps with an existing reservation for the same room ID, utilizing database-level locking,live updates could show users live status of the particular room (at the one only available edge case).  
* **REQ-RES-04:** The system allows registered users or members to allocate their reward points and include any offers to the type and criteria the offer applies to.  
* **REQ-RES-05:** The system shall automatically update a room's status to "Occupied" upon check-in and "Cleaning" (or "Available") upon check-out.

### **4.5 Service Management**

**4.5.1 Description and Priority** Medium Priority. This module manages the internal catalogue of chargeable amenities and tracks their consumption by guests during an active stay to facilitate progressive billing.

**4.5.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* **Service Usage Logging:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A guest orders room service; staff logs the service to the room.  
  * **Response:** The system records the usage, locking in the current price of the service, and adds it to the guest's progressive bill.

**4.5.3 Functional Requirements**

* **REQ-SRV-01:** The system shall maintain a centralized Service Catalogue containing the name, description, and current base price of all chargeable amenities.  
* **REQ-SRV-02:** The system shall allow authorized staff to log service usage to a specific active booking.  
* **REQ-SRV-03:** The system must record the exact price of the service *at the time of usage* to prevent historical billing discrepancies if catalogue prices change later.

### 

### 

### **4.6 Billing and Payments**

**4.6.1 Description and Priority** High Priority. This module oversees the financial ledger, aggregates charges, enforces Sri Lankan statutory tax formulas, and restricts check-outs for unpaid dues.

**4.6.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* **Partial Payment Processing:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A guest makes a mid-stay partial payment at the front desk.  
  * **Response:** The system records the payment, deducts it from the running total, and leaves the booking flagged with an "Outstanding Balance".  
* **Final Check-Out Attempt:**  
  * **Stimulus:** Staff attempt to check out a guest with an outstanding balance.  
  * **Response:** The system denies the state transition until the final calculated total is paid.

**4.6.3 Functional Requirements**

* **REQ-BIL-01:** The system shall calculate the final bill using a sequential tax formula (10% Service Charge, 1% TDL, 2.5% SSCL, and 18% VAT) strictly executed via a database stored procedure (`sp_Generate_Final_Bill`).  
* **Billing & Tax Calculation Formulas (with no offers or card discounts):**  
*        **Base** \= (Daily Rate × Nights) \+ Σ Services **Service Charge** \= Base × 0.10 **TDL** \= Base × 0.01 **SSCL** \= Base × 0.025 **VAT** \= (Base \+ TDL \+ SSCL) × 0.18 **Total** \= Base \+ Service Charge \+ TDL \+ SSCL \+ VAT

* **REQ-BIL-02:** The system shall accept partial payments during a guest's stay and dynamically calculate the remaining outstanding balance.  
* **REQ-BIL-03:** The system shall actively prevent the transition of a booking status to "Checked-Out" if the associated Bill object possesses an outstanding balance greater than zero.

### **4.7 Guest Loyalty/Membership Program Management**

**4.7.1 Description and Priority** Medium Priority. This module incentivizes repeat visits through a point-based tier system. It includes a specific points-expiration mechanic to encourage continuous engagement.

**4.7.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* **Post-Stay Point Allocation:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A registered member successfully checks out with a fully paid bill.  
  * **Response:** The system automatically calculates points based on total money spent and stay duration, adding them to the Guest Profile.  
* **Annual Point Expiration:**  
  * **Stimulus:** A background system timer (CRON job) detects points earned exactly 365 days ago.  
  * **Response:** The system automatically deducts those expired points from the user's active balance and recalculates their current tier.

**4.7.3 Functional Requirements**

* **REQ-LOY-01:** The system shall award loyalty points to registered members upon the completion of a fully paid stay.  
* **REQ-LOY-02:** The system shall dynamically categorize members into Silver, Gold, or Platinum tiers based on their active point balance.  
* **REQ-LOY-03:** The system shall enforce a strict 1-year (365 days) expiration policy on all earned points, automatically deducting them from the guest's profile one year after they were awarded.  
* **REQ-LOY-04:** The system shall automatically apply tier-specific discounts and seasonal promotional rates to a member's direct bookings.

### **4.8 Reporting**

**4.8.1 Description and Priority** Medium Priority. An administrative analytics module providing upper management with data-driven insights into branch performance and revenue streams.

**4.8.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* **Revenue Generation Request:**  
  * **Stimulus:** An Admin requests the "Monthly Revenue Report."  
  * **Response:** The system aggregates SQL data and displays total revenue segmented by room charges and service usage.

**4.8.3 Functional Requirements**

* **REQ-RPT-01:** The system shall generate an accurate room occupancy report for any user-selected date or date range across all branches.  
* **REQ-RPT-02:** The system shall generate a guest billing summary specifically highlighting unpaid balances.  
* **REQ-RPT-03:** The system shall calculate and visualize monthly revenue per branch, distinctly separating room revenue from service catalogue revenue.  
* **REQ-RPT-04:** The system, under the respective individuals approvals, should allow the system to include new offers and other offers to the system for the guests/members to receive and apply them as necessary.

***5\. Other Nonfunctional Requirements***

***5.1 Performance Requirements***

***Response Time Requirements***

* *The system shall display the login page and dashboard within **2-3 seconds** under normal network conditions.*  
* *The system shall complete room reservation, check-in, check-out, and payment transactions within **4 seconds** under normal operating conditions.*  
* *The system shall retrieve room availability and guest information within **3 seconds**.*  
* *The system shall generate occupancy, billing, and revenue reports within **8 seconds**.*

***Capacity and Scalability Requirements***

* *The system shall support at least **75 concurrent users** without significant degradation in response time.*  
* *The system shall maintain acceptable performance as additional hotel branches, rooms, guests, and bookings are added.*  
* *Database operations shall maintain consistent performance under normal daily hotel workloads.*

 

***5.2 Safety Requirements***

***Data Protection and Recovery***

* *The system shall perform automatic database backups every **6 hours**, with a complete backup generated **once every day**.*  
* *In the event of a system failure, the database shall be restored with a maximum data loss of **6 hours**.*  
*  *The system shall validate all user inputs before storing them in the database to minimize invalid or inconsistent records.*  
*  *Database transactions shall be protected to ensure data consistency during unexpected interruptions.*

 

 

***Fault Recovery***

* *The system shall resume normal operation as quickly as possible after hardware or software failures.*

***Monitoring***

* *The system shall maintain logs of critical errors and system events to assist in troubleshooting and maintenance.*

 

***5.3 Security Requirements***

***Authentication and Authorization***

* *All staff members shall authenticate before accessing the system.*  
* *The system shall enforce role-based access control with the following user roles:*  
  * ***Receptionist** – Manage guest registration, reservations, check-in, check-out, and payments.*  
  * ***Service Staff** – Record guest service requests and service usage.*  
  * ***Manager** – Access reports, manage room rates, services, and branch operations.*  
  * ***Administrator** – Full system administration, user management, and configuration.*  
* *Passwords shall be securely stored using modern password hashing algorithms.*

***Data Security***

* *Sensitive guest information and payment details shall be encrypted while stored in the database.*  
* *All communication between the client application and server shall use secure HTTPS connections.*  
* *Access to guest information shall be limited to authorized personnel only.*

***Audit Logging***

* *The system shall record user login attempts, booking updates, payment transactions, cancellations, and administrative activities.*  
* *Audit logs shall include the user ID, date and time, and the action performed.*

 

***5.4 Software Quality Attributes***

***Reliability***

* *The system shall maintain at least **99% operational availability**, excluding scheduled maintenance.*  
* *All booking and payment transactions shall follow ACID principles to maintain database consistency.*  
* *The system shall recover incomplete transactions without compromising stored data.*

***Usability***

* *New reception staff shall be able to perform standard hotel operations after **one working day** of training.*  
* *Frequently used functions such as booking, guest search, and payment processing shall be easily accessible through the main dashboard.*  
* *The system shall display meaningful validation and error messages to guide users during data entry.*

***Accessibility***

* *The application shall support keyboard navigation and operate correctly on modern web browsers.*  
* *The user interface shall use clear fonts, appropriate colour contrast, and consistent layouts to improve readability.*

***Maintainability***

* *The software shall follow a modular architecture to simplify future maintenance and feature enhancements.*  
* *Technical documentation shall include the database schema, system architecture, and deployment instructions.*  
* *The source code shall follow consistent coding standards and naming conventions.*

***Scalability***

* *The system shall support future expansion to additional hotel branches without major modifications to the software architecture.*  

***Compatibility***

* *The system shall operate on Windows and Linux servers and be accessible through current versions of Chrome, Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Safari.*

 

***5.5 Business Rules***

***Reservation Rules***

* *A room shall not be assigned to multiple bookings that overlap for the same reservation period.*  
* *The check-out date shall always be later than the corresponding check-in date.*  
* *Only rooms marked as **Available** may be reserved.*  
* *Cancelling a reservation shall immediately make the room available for future bookings.*

***Guest Stay Rules***

* *The room status shall automatically change to **Occupied** when a guest checks in.*  
* *The room status shall automatically change to **Available** after a successful check-out.*  
* *Standard check-in and check-out times shall be configurable by hotel management.*  
* *Early check-in and late check-out requests shall be subject to room availability and hotel policy.*

***Billing and Payment Rules***

* *Every service consumed by a guest shall be linked to an active booking.*  
* *Room charges shall be calculated based on the applicable daily room rate and the number of nights stayed.*  
* *The final bill shall include accommodation charges and all recorded service charges.*  
*  *The system shall support partial payments while maintaining the remaining outstanding balance.*  
* *A booking shall not be completed until payment has been settled or any outstanding balance has been recorded according to hotel policy.*

***Operational Rules***

* *Guests shall present a valid government-issued identification document during check-in.*  
* *Every payment transaction shall be associated with an existing booking record.*  
* *Monthly revenue reports shall separately summarize room revenue and service revenue for each hotel branch.*

## **Appendix A: Relational Database Specification**

This section outlines the planned architectural methodology for the backend database. To ensure data integrity, eliminate redundancy, and guarantee transactional reliability, the project will strictly adhere to Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) and enforce ACID compliance directly at the database level.

### **6.1 Planned BCNF Normalization & Functional Dependencies**

The system's relational schema will be designed such that for every non-trivial functional dependency X \-\> Y, the determinant  must be a superkey. To demonstrate this planned compliance, the following core target schemas and their dependencies will be implemented:

**1\. Room\_Type Relation**

* **Target Schema:** `Room_Type(type_id, type_name, capacity, daily_rate, amenities)`  
* **Functional Dependency: type\_id \-\> type\_name, capacity, daily\_rate, amenities**  
* **Design Rationale:** By establishing type\_id as the primary candidate key, the design will successfully separate overarching room category details from individual room instances, thereby preventing the redundant storage of daily rates and capacities.

**2\. Room Relation**

* **Target Schema:** `Room(room_id, branch_id, room_number, type_id, current_status)`  
* **Functional Dependencies:**  
  * **room\_id \-\> branch\_id, room\_number, type\_id, current\_status**  
  * branch\_id, room\_number-\> room\_id  
* **Design Rationale:** The schema will enforce that both single and composite determinants act as candidate keys, firmly satisfying BCNF requirements for inventory tracking.

**3\. Guest\_Loyalty Relation**

* **Target Schema:** `Guest_Loyalty(tier_id, tier_name, min_points, discount_percentage)`  
* **Functional Dependency: tier\_id \-\> tier\_name, min\_points, discount\_percentage**  
* **Design Rationale:** This relation will isolate loyalty parameters from individual guest records, ensuring that future updates to tier discounts or point thresholds do not require cascading updates across the entire guest database.

### **6.2 Planned Database Procedures, Functions, and Triggers**

Rather than relying solely on the application layer (Node.js) for critical business logic, the project will implement a robust suite of database-level objects. This methodology ensures that concurrency control and Sri Lankan tax compliance are baked directly into the data layer.

The following table serves as the specification blueprint for the procedures, functions, and triggers that will be developed to maintain ACID compliance:

| Planned Object Name | Object Type | Intended Purpose & ACID Role |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **`sp_CreateBooking()`** | Stored Procedure | Will encapsulate the booking creation process within an isolated ACID transaction. It is planned to utilize `FOR UPDATE` locks on room availability records to explicitly prevent race conditions during simultaneous direct or OTA booking requests. |
| **`sp_Generate_Final_Bill()`** | Stored Procedure | Will query base room and service charges to dynamically calculate statutory taxes (10% SC, 1% TDL, 2.5% SSCL, and 18% VAT). This sequential calculation will be executed within a single transaction before committing the finalized aggregated bill record. |
| **`function_Check_Room_Availability()`** | Stored Function | Will be designed to evaluate date ranges and return a boolean (`TRUE`/`FALSE`) indicating whether a specific room ID possesses overlapping reservations. |
| **`trigger_Prevent_Double_Booking`** | `BEFORE INSERT` Trigger | Will act as a fail-safe on the `Booking` table. Before any row is committed, it will call `fn_Check_Room_Availability()` and forcibly raise a custom SQL exception to halt the transaction if a date overlap is detected. |
| **`trigger_Auto_Update_Loyalty_Tier`** | `AFTER UPDATE` Trigger | Will monitor the `Payment` table. Upon a status change to 'COMPLETED', it will automatically trigger a recalculation of the guest's accumulated points and update their respective membership tier (Silver, Gold, Platinum). |

;

### 

### **6.3 Planned Database Population & Seed Data Strategy**

To rigorously validate the system's functional requirements, structural integrity, and ACID compliance, the development environment will be initialized with a dummy dataset. This planned data population strategy ensures all edge cases are checked—particularly those involving concurrent bookings, tier logic, and complex billing. It later can be effectively tested prior to production deployment.

The seeding specification will encompass the following entities:

* **Hotel Branches:** The system will initialize with three operational branches (Colombo, Kandy, Galle). The Colombo branch will be specifically configured to test the baseline regulatory minimum room rate ($100) constraints applicable to 5-star properties within CMC limits.  
* **Room Inventory:** A minimum of 10 distinct room records will be instantiated across various categories (Single, Double, Suite). Each will be mapped to specific daily rates and capacity limits to validate referential integrity against the `Room_Type` schema.  
* **Service Catalogue:** The initial database state will include a baseline of 6 chargeable services (e.g., Spa Treatment, Laundry Service, Minibar Refill, Room Service Dining, Airport Transfer, Executive Lounge Access). This will allow testers to validate progressive bill calculations and the dynamic application of Sri Lankan tax levies on amenities.  
* **Guest & Booking Simulation:** The database will be seeded with 5 diverse guest profiles spanning varying baseline loyalty tiers. To validate overlap logic and temporal constraints, 8 booking records will be procedurally generated, encompassing a mix of historical, currently active, and future stay dates.  
* **Financial & Transactional Testing Scenarios:** To simulate real-world operations, the seeding script will populate mock room availability logs and dynamic service usage entries. Crucially, the dataset will include at least 3 scripted **partial payment scenarios** to explicitly test the `Bill` object's outstanding balance flags and guarantee that the check-out restriction logic holds firm under fractional payment conditions.
